solutionSql:
SELECT d.shipment_id, COUNT(*)::integer AS distinct_scans
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT sc.shipment_id, sc.status, sc.occurred_at
  FROM staging_scans AS sc
  JOIN shipments AS s ON s.id = sc.shipment_id
  WHERE sc.status IS NOT NULL
) AS d
GROUP BY d.shipment_id
ORDER BY d.shipment_id;

ambiguities.phrase: two scans are the same when they have the same status and occurred_at
ambiguities.readingChosen: Scans with the same shipment, status and occurred_at are one scan; a NULL occurred_at is a value, so two same-status scans with NULL occurred_at count once and a NULL-time scan still counts (SELECT DISTINCT semantics).
ambiguities.alternativeReading: A scan with NULL occurred_at is not counted (as COUNT(DISTINCT occurred_at) would ignore it), or each NULL-time scan counts separately.

ambiguities.phrase: A scan for a shipment that does not exist is not counted
ambiguities.readingChosen: Keep only scans whose shipment_id matches shipments.id; a NULL shipment_id is also dropped.
ambiguities.alternativeReading: None material; a NULL shipment_id could be read as its own group, but it is not an existing shipment.

notes: De-duplicate on (shipment_id, status, occurred_at) after dropping NULL-status and orphan scans, then count per shipment cast to integer. Sample: 41 scans, 5 orphans, 3 NULL-status on real shipments, one duplicate on shipment 120, giving 32 rows of count 1. Scan id is ignored for duplicate detection.
